partners.mechanism_chain: HSD17B4 (HGNC:5213) —DISRUPTS→ Fatty acid beta-oxidation and bile acid synthesis (REACT:R-HSA-8963684); Fatty acid beta-oxidation and bile acid synthesis (REACT:R-HSA-8963684) —LEADS_TO→ Peroxisomal dysfunction (HP:0001250); Fatty acid beta-oxidation and bile acid synthesis (REACT:R-HSA-8963684) —LEADS_TO→ Ovarian dysgenesis (HP:0000099); Fatty acid beta-oxidation and bile acid synthesis (REACT:R-HSA-8963684) —LEADS_TO→ Cerebellar hypoplasia (HP:0001324). Loss-of-function mutations in HSD17B4 disrupt fatty acid beta-oxidation and bile acid synthesis pathways. This disruption leads to peroxisomal dysfunction, which underlies the various phenotypes observed in d-bifunctional protein deficiency, including cerebellar hypoplasia. Concurrently, the disruption of these pathways also affects ovarian development, leading to ovarian dysgenesis, a key feature of Perrault syndrome 1. The shared disruption of these fundamental metabolic pathways by the same gene explains the overlap in disease mechanisms.

This disruption leads to peroxisomal dysfunction, which underlies the various phenotypes observed in d-bifunctional protein deficiency, including cerebellar hypoplasia.
